title: tooling(gates): check-new-cross-file-line-citations cannot parse the bare :NNN continuation form its charter claims — it reports 0 on a docblock whose six citations had all rotted
body:
Found twice today by two independent seats working objectui#8990, and measured the second time. ⛔ Not a defect in any PR — a defect in the gate.

## The finding

`check-new-cross-file-line-citations` reports **`0 new citation(s)`** on a diff whose docblock carries **six cross-file line citations**, all of which had already **rotted**.

The six sat in the `ObjectKanbanSchema.groupBy` docblock pointing into `ObjectKanban.tsx` — `:601` `:613` `:625` `:640` `:747` `:865`. Measured on the merge base: the reads they name now sit **~370 lines lower**. Every one was stale, and the gate scored the diff clean.

## The mechanism, measured

`census.mjs:569-576` only parses a bare `:NNN` **within 2 lines of a numbered hit**. On that docblock it finds **0 of the six** addresses — while the gate's own charter claims to cover 「无文件名的续写地址」 (continuation addresses with no filename), which is exactly the form these six use.

⇒ **The gate is not report-only about this class. It is silent on it.** Those are different things, and only the first is a deliberate policy choice. A report-only gate that cannot parse the form it claims to watch reports a clean sheet, and a reader who knows it is report-only still reads that as "nothing new to look at".

## Why it matters here specifically

⭐ This is the gate that exists to stop line citations from rotting, and the form that rotted is the form it cannot see. The failure is self-concealing: the rot accumulates precisely where the instrument is blind, and the instrument's output says everything is fine.

⚠️ It also mislabels its own coverage. A gate whose charter names a class it does not parse is worse than a gate that says nothing, because it is cited as evidence — objectui#8990's dev correctly declined to file on the grounds that "the gate already owns this class", which is true of the charter and false of the code.

## What is owed

1. **Make the parser see the bare `:NNN` continuation form**, or **narrow the charter** so it stops claiming a class it does not cover. ⛔ Not both silently — pick one and say which.
2. Either way, a **firing control**: a fixture carrying the exact six-address shape from that docblock, asserting the gate now reports them. ⛔ A green run proves nothing here; the whole finding is that green was the wrong answer.
3. ⚠️ **Measure the backlog before changing the parser.** If it starts seeing this form, how many existing citations does it light up? That number decides whether the gate can go enforcing or must stay report-only for a while — and it is the number nobody has.

## ⚠️ Not measured

- Whether other citation forms are also unparsed (only the bare `:NNN` continuation form was measured).
- How many rotted citations exist tree-wide in this form — see item 3, which is the same gap.
- Whether the 2-line proximity window is deliberate (it may be guarding against false positives, in which case the fix is charter-side, not parser-side).
- The gate's workflow trigger conditions.

Refs objectui#8990 (where both readings were taken) · objectui#8924 (the installed-spec-pin claim rotting in ~53 places — same family: an anchor that drifts and a gate that does not catch it).
